question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: Round 2 of the panel (opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol) on record 2026-10-03-markdown-table-cell-blocks-again found that the narrowed cascade breaks spanning cells, the List decoder drops trailing item breaks, editors without List would regress, the private tree shape and grammar details were unspecified, the image-item claim was false and D8 was settled by citing docs. This record applies those findings; two applied-critical rounds reached the panel cap.
requirements: Preserve representable Markdown meaning in GFM table cells; diagnose intentional or unsupported loss and obey lossPolicy.
A GFM row stays on one line and keeps its column geometry: no cell content writes a raw newline, and no fallback shifts a surviving cell into another column.
Features own their mappings: the List feature builds list paragraphs; the Markdown runtime owns intrinsic syntax and keeps non-standard tree shapes private.
Keep Markdown parsing DOM-free and keep the selective registered-tag grammar; editors without the List feature keep the literal fallback for list HTML in cells.

Read the Markdown Plate ships on main: VISION.md preserves serialized-data laws, and @platejs/markdown released PR 5139 (961c65be4c, then Version packages ef90c27119), which writes cell lists as inline
    ,
      and
    1. HTML, task items in
        with a leading and one space, and cell breaks as
        . The verdict also holds on GFM renderability and losslessness alone.
evidenceReuse: Reused both earlier records' probes, main's encoder and the docs contract. Round 2 seats ran read-only probes that injected the proposed list shape into a table cell (trailing break lost, List-absent parse failure, span column shift); their findings are in the decision log beside the review page.
summary:
Pursue, with the target constrained by two panel rounds. On next, a cell holding list paragraphs refuses and the refusal cascades through the row and the table: under the default lossPolicy reject the serialize fails and copy writes no text/markdown, and under allow the whole table disappears. A break inside a cell paragraph becomes a space with no diagnostic, a trailing break writes a raw newline into the row, and main's released cell-list HTML reads on next as literal text. On parse, when a list decoder is installed, a rewrite in the remarkToSlate compiler, after user remark plugins, turns a tableCell's HTML run (
    ,
      ,
    1. , lists nested in
    2. , and in
        only a leading with bare checked or disabled and one following space) into a private list shape the List decoder builds paragraphs from; trailing breaks inside an item survive or are diagnosed; without a list decoder the run stays literal. On serialize, a typed runtime helper on the Markdown encode context turns a cell's children into phrasing (HTML tokens and
        ), owns main's rule of
        only between two non-list segments and the newlines inside list items, and replaces the cell mapping's own
        join; parse-only passes stay off serialize. In the cascade, a content refusal in an unspanned cell keeps its column as an empty cell with a lossy diagnostic; a span flattens through the table grid (content in the anchor slot, empty covered slots, one lossy diagnostic) or keeps the table refusal. A captioned or attributed image in a cell list refuses through that cascade or flattens to phrasing with its own loss report. The plan decides whether raw HTML that no mapping accepts is lossless, as the shipped docs say, or lossy, as D8 says, given that a cell list round-trips to escaped tag text with no diagnostic today. It also decides which signal paragraph folding into
        gets.

callSites.current: No public call changes. Today the table cell markdown.encode runs encode(children); a list paragraph group returns an mdast list, so the cell refuses, the row and the table refuse in turn, and serialize fails under reject or drops the table under allow. The cell encoder spreads paragraph children into the row, so a break becomes a space and a trailing break writes a raw newline. On parse, <ul><li> in a cell stays literal text with one lossless warning per tag.

reconciliation.question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Parse-only passes stay off serialize and the per-operation context cache stays; the cell helper must keep both.

alternatives: Keep refusing: loses. It is honest about loss but fails every export of a document with a list in any cell and drops the whole table under allow.

Flatten list paragraphs into paragraphs joined by
with markdown-property-omitted warnings: viable fallback that keeps text and explicit loss, but it drops structure GFM viewers render from HTML.

Runtime decoder that rebuilds list paragraphs from a cell's HTML (the first record's target): superseded. It duplicates the List feature's decode, including restart and start logic, which is how main's table rules drifted.

Reuse the feature HTML mappings to write and read HTML in cells: Stop. The Markdown mapping contract exposes no HTML encode or decode, although every editor compiles the HTML artifact. Saved probes show HTML serialize writes one <ul>/<ol> per item with data-* attributes and margin styles and leaves | and raw newlines inside <li>, each of which breaks a GFM row; HTML parse needs a DOM that Markdown parsing avoids and ignores <input type="checkbox"> task markup.

Register ul, ol and li as Plate tags: Stop. Lists are native Markdown outside cells, so registering them would claim raw list HTML everywhere; D9 also demotes registered block tags inside a tableCell.

Runtime syntax transform between a cell's HTML list run and the List decoder, with a private tree shape, a List-installed gate, a typed phrasing helper for serialize, main's grammar rules and a span-safe cascade: Pursue. The List and Table mappings keep their ownership, mdast types stay standard outside the runtime, GFM viewers render lists (task checkboxes on github.com unverified) and main's released output reads back.
proofLimits: Source inspection, headless probes against the platejs dist built on 2026-10-02 and the next source, and main's merged encoder read at a8607621c0. Every probe cited has saved output. No browser, clipboard, GitHub rendering check, package suite or Benchmark run, and no prototype of the mdast-level transform. Reading main's output is argued from its encoder and a hand-written cell, not a corpus of main exports. Round-2 seat probes injected the proposed shape into the compiled runtime; no prototype of the rewrite, helper or grid-aware cascade exists. Whether github.com renders raw <input type="checkbox"> in a cell is unverified. The constraints in this record were applied after the second panel round and were not reviewed by a further round. Evidence lives in gitignored docs/plans/artifacts, as in earlier records of this scope.
